title: God's Hidden Care
lead: The Bible's teaching that God guides events, even when he is unseen and unnamed, through ordinary choices, "chance" and human plans. It is clearest in the stories of Joseph, Ruth and Esther, and in sayings like "People throw the lot into the lap, / but every verdict it gives comes from the LORD" (Proverbs 16:33). How God's guidance fits with human freedom and with evil is debated: Augustinian and Reformed theologians, Arminian and Wesleyan theologians, and open theists give different answers.

sections.b: Joseph tells his brothers, "You planned evil against me, but God planned it for good" (Genesis 50:20). Proverbs teaches that "a person's heart maps out his road, / but the LORD fixes where his steps fall" (Proverbs 16:9). Esther never mentions God at all, yet Mordecai asks whether Esther came to the throne "for a time like this" (Esther 4:14). Jesus speaks of the Father's care for sparrows and the hairs of the head (Matthew 10:29–31), and Paul says God works all things together for good for those who love him (Romans 8:28). These texts agree that God acts through ordinary events; they do not settle the later debates about how.
sections.refs: Genesis 50:20; Proverbs 16:9; Proverbs 16:33; Esther 4:14; Matthew 10:29–31; Romans 8:28
